legend: A permutation is a sequence of length n%%ZSMJ0%% consisting of integers from 1%%ZSMJ1%% to n%%ZSMJ2%%, in which all the numbers occur exactly once. For example, [1]%%ZSMJ3%%, [3,5,2,1,4]%%ZSMJ4%%, and [1,3,2]%%ZSMJ5%% are permutations, whereas [2,3,2]%%ZSMJ6%%, [4,3,1]%%ZSMJ7%%, and [0]%%ZSMJ8%% are not.

You are given an array A1,A2,…,AN%%ZSMJ9%% consisting of N%%ZSMJ10%% integers. Each integer is 0%%ZSMJ11%% or 1%%ZSMJ12%%. Find the number of permutations P%%ZSMJ13%% of size N%%ZSMJ14%% such that the following conditions hold:
A_{P_i} \equiv i \pmod{2}%%ZSMJ16%%, for all (1 \leq i \leq N%%ZSMJ17%%).
Because the number of such permutations can be very large, print the answer modulo 998244353%%ZSMJ18%%.
input: The first line contains an integer N \ (1 \leq N \leq 10^6)%%ZSMJ19%%.
The second line contains N%%ZSMJ20%% space separated integers A_i%%ZSMJ21%% - the elements of the array. It's guaranteed that A_i \in \{0, 1\}%%ZSMJ22%%.
output: Output a single line containing the number of permutations satisfying the conditions modulo 998244353%%ZSMJ23%%.
